rationale: Greek/Latin loanword φόσσα/fossa 'trench, ditch.' Used here for the three cosmic fossae prepared as binding-pits for the dark powers. Standard Manichaean cosmographic feature. Preserve as 'fossa' (transliterated) to retain technical specificity.

Greek πεῖρας 'boundary, limit.' Used here in the cosmological phrase ⲡⲡⲓⲣⲁⲥ ⲛⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ 'the boundary of the sea' — the cosmic sea-boundary set by the Father of Life. Cf. Job 38:8-11 (LXX πεῖρας) for biblical parallel.
Greek σφαῖρα 'sphere.' Standard cosmological term for the celestial sphere from which the boundary of the sea is brought forth.
Greek τοῖχος 'wall.' Cosmic bounding structure set by the Father of Life in the great sea. Distinct from κόσμος (whole world-system) and στερέωμα (firmament). Confidence moderate.
Greek πλέω 'sail.' Used here of the cosmic light-ships (sun and moon) sailing in the great sea. Standard nautical verb in Manichaean cosmographic context.

Likely from ⲡⲱⲣϣ̄ 'spread out' substantivized as 'expanse, spreading.' The 'great expanse' that draws Matter into the midst of the worlds — possibly a cosmographic structure between the upper and lower regions. Confidence moderate.

Tentative: Lyc. reflex of ϩⲁⲏ 'rear, end, last part.' Paired with ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ 'Error' as a negative cosmic principle to be driven from creation. 'Dregs of the Darkness' captures the sense of residual evil being expelled. Confidence low.

Greek ἀνώγαιον 'upper room.' Used here cosmologically of 'the seven of the upper-place' = the seven firmaments. Distinct from ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ (general 'above') by being a more architectural-cosmological term. Confidence moderate.

Greek κνώψ 'noxious creeping creature' (or κνέφας 'gloom'). Used in cosmic-fauna inventory alongside clouds, winds, spirits, and birds. The dark cosmic beings inhabiting the gloomy regions outside the seven firmaments.

proposed_english: (uncertain — possibly garments or class of dark beings)
rationale: Lexeme of unclear identity. Plural form, contextually a class of beings or coverings that 'are clothed' (ⲃⲱⲟⲥ) in the archontic host. Flagged for further parallels.
Plural of ⲥⲟⲃⲧⲉ 'preparation, defenses.' Cosmic structures/enclosures bounding the great sea within which the ships sail.
Possibly variant of ⲡϣⲓⲭϩ 'abyss' (already in vocab) or related to ⲡⲱϫϩ 'split, break.' Used here of the cosmic pit into which the dark powers are cast down. Confidence low.
Lyc. reflex of ⲥⲱⲛϩ̄ 'bind, chain.' Distinct from ⲥⲁⲛⲟⲩϣ 'nourish' (different root). Forms the doublet 'bind-and-chain' (ⲙⲟⲩⲣ + ⲥⲱⲛϩ̄) for the imprisonment of dark powers in the cosmic fossae.
